fact: Our planetary system is called “the solar system” because we use the word “solar” to describe things related to our star, after the Latin word for Sun, "solis."
Our solar system orbits the center of the Milky Way galaxy at about 515,000 mph (829,000 kph).
It takes our solar system about 230 million years to complete one orbit around the galactic center.
The hottest planet in our solar system is Venus, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
The largest planet is Jupiter. If Jupiter was a hollow shell, 1,000 Earths could fit inside.
There are hundreds of moons in our solar system. Most orbit planets, but some asteroids have moons.
The four giant planets–and at least one asteroid–have rings. None are as spectacular as Saturn’s gorgeous rings.
More than 300 robotic spacecraft from many nations have explored destinations beyond Earth’s orbit.
Our solar system is the only one known to support life. So far, we only know of life on Earth, but we’re looking for more everywhere we can.
NASA’s Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 are the only spacecraft leaving our solar system. Three other spacecraft – Pioneer 10, Pioneer 11, and New Horizons – will eventually hit interstellar space.
